Theoretical

/thee-uh-RET-ih-kul/ — punch the RET: 'theo-RET-ical' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Theoretical is based on ideas and reasoning rather than practical experience.

Her knowledge of sailing was purely theoretical until she finally stepped onto a boat.

Worked Example

The engineering students designed a solar-powered car on paper, calculating exactly how fast it should go. But none of them had ever built one, and their numbers had never touched a real road.

Their design was theoretical — based on ideas and reasoning rather than hands-on experience. 'Practical' knowledge comes from doing; theoretical knowledge lives in models, formulas, and untested plans.

How Theoretical Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

hypothetical

hypothetical: assumed for the sake of argument, not proven real

abstract

abstract: existing in thought rather than physical form

speculative

speculative: based on guesswork rather than evidence

Antonyms

practical

practical: based on real use and experience

concrete

concrete: real, specific, and tangible

How Strong Is It? — unproven → imaginary → theoretical

unproven vs. theoretical

unproven vs. theoretical: Unproven is weaker than theoretical — an unproven idea merely lacks final confirmation, while a theoretical one may never have left the world of ideas at all.

imaginary vs. theoretical

imaginary vs. theoretical: Imaginary is stronger than theoretical — a theoretical idea is a serious untested model, but an imaginary one exists only in fantasy with no basis in reasoning.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

root — theor-

root — theor-: to look at, contemplate (Greek)

suffix — -ical

suffix — -ical: relating to (Greek/Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Greek theoria meant 'a viewing or contemplation.' Theoretical knowledge is what you gain by looking at and thinking about something, rather than by doing it.

Use the root in a new word: theorem

Use the root in a new word: theorem: The class proved the geometry theorem using only three earlier rules.
